Six bullets, six rungs, all of them real actions. Everything under them is commentary: the Vanono line in Kazham under bullet 2 is flavour text the page itself labels Optional, and the three Tome of Magic under bullet 5 are lore excerpts, not inspections the mission needs. Bullet 4's 'Travel to the Temple of Uggalepih' is folded into the fight rather than given a travel rung of its own, because the bullet is one journey to one NM.

EVIDENCE, two rungs of it. The Cursed Key at step 4 is an ordinary item (1143), held and then spent at step 5, so it is legal on step 4 only. The page warns it will not drop if you already hold one -- which means a player who arrives already carrying a Cursed Key reads step 4 as done. That is the RIGHT answer rather than a bug: holding the key is the entire point of the rung, and the mark moves to the Granite Door, which is where such a player should go.

The Book of the Gods at step 5 is not in Reward (Rank 8 and 60,000 gil), so it is usable. One caution recorded rather than hidden: res/key_items.lua carries BOTH 251 'blank Book of the Gods' and 252 'Book of the Gods'. The page says '[KI] Book of the Gods', so 252 is what is written. If the game actually grants 251 the rung simply never fires and the mark lags on the Granite Door, which is the safe direction; it cannot send anyone anywhere wrong.

Step 6 lists the Book of the Gods in items rather than evidence -- it is what you must be holding to close the mission out, and it is already step 5's evidence, which hard rule 4 forbids repeating.

Thirteen bullets become sixteen rungs. Bullet 2 splits into three, one per minister, because the page says 'in any order' outright -- they share the group 'ministry_rings' and each gets its own zone, which is the whole point since they are in Fei'Yin, Davoi and Windurst Waters. Bullet 7 splits into a pop and a fight, and bullet 8 is the third click on the same wall; that is one sentence describing three distinct things a player does. The optional returns to Shantotto and Tosuka-Porika under bullet 13 are flavour dialogue and are not rungs.

RUKUSUSU IS NOT THE TARGET IN FEI'YIN. The page says to click the Cermet Door of the north-western small room 'for a cutscene with her' -- she is in the cutscene, the door is the entity, so the door carries the marker and her name is in the note. Same reasoning as Carbuncle in the Summoner AF quests.

EVIDENCE, and the one genuinely hard call on this page. All five ministry rings are real key items (Manustery 281, Rhinostery 280, Aurastery 276, Optistery 250, Orastery 265) and none of them is in Reward (Rank 9 and 80,000 gil), so all are usable in principle. But two things constrain where they go.

First, the group. The runtime has NO notion of a group: core/steps.lua computes position as 1 + max{i : evidence(i) true}, a high-water maximum over a linear ladder. Put one ring on each of the three group members and a player who visits Sedal-Godjal first jumps the mark to member three and then sticks there forever, because member three would have nothing left to prove. So the whole AND-list rides the LAST group member, exactly as An Explorer's Footsteps does with its Clay Tablet: holding all three rings is what moves the mark out of the group and on to Apururu, and holding one or two moves nothing. The cost is that the mark lags at step 1 during collection; lagging is the safe direction.

Second, the Optistery ring is the SAME key item Windurst 7-1 hands out -- one id, 250, and the 7-1 page in this same lane says you receive it there. I cannot observe whether the game takes it back, so it is deliberately INSIDE the AND-list rather than left out: if it does persist, an AND-list of all three is still false until the other two are collected, whereas an AND-list of only the other two would fire the moment they were, skipping Tosuka-Porika every single time. Including it is strictly the safer of the two. Flagged ki_shared_with_earlier_mission.

Note also that the AND-list makes the ring-to-minister mapping irrelevant: the page lists three ministers and three rings without pairing them, and 'hold all three' does not need the pairing. That removed the last guess from this record.

The remaining evidence rungs are ordinary: Manustery ring at step 1, Orastery ring at step 11, glove of perpetual twilight at step 13, each granted at its own rung and nowhere else in this mission.

Eight walkthrough bullets and an 'After the walkthrough: BCNM' section that holds the END of the mission, not notes. Its bullets [7] and [8] -- return to the Door: Vestal Chamber, then click it again for the final cutscene 'to end the Windurst story line' -- are the last thing a player does and would have been lost if the section were treated as commentary. Its bullets [1]-[3] are Windower/FastCS troubleshooting (unload enternity, FrameRateDivisor, click the glowing spot outside the tower if you crashed) and its bullet [6] is optional dialogue; none of those are rungs. Bullets [4] and [5] are the two halves of the BCNM and become two fight rungs. Flagged steps_from_after_section, and every affected note says which section it came from -- the After section's numbering restarts at [1], so source_bullets cites the walkthrough bullet the rung continues from.

Walkthrough bullet 1 is optional dialogue and is not a rung. Bullet 3 is a heading for bullets 4-6 -- 'Collect the following 3 Key Items in any order' -- so those three share the group 'verses' and each cites [3] alongside its own bullet.

TYPO CORRECTED. Bullet 4 writes 'Qu'Hua Spring' in Ro'Maeve at (H-6). The Windurst 8-1 page in this same lane, and the existing Divine Might record, both name the same object at the same coordinates 'Qu'Hau Spring'. Two spellings, one object; the majority form is written and the page's spelling is recorded here. Both fold to distinct keys, so this is the difference between a marker and none.

THE THREE KEY ITEMS ARE NOT NAMED ON THE PAGE, and I named them anyway -- this is the judgement call to check. The page says only 'the following 3 Key Items' at Ro'Maeve, the Chamber of Oracles and the Temple of Uggalepih. res/key_items.lua -- the game client's own table, not another wiki page -- carries exactly three consecutive entries, 478 'Ancient Verse of Ro'Maeve', 479 'Ancient Verse of Altepa' and 480 'Ancient Verse of Uggalepih'. Two of the three name the page's own locations outright, and the third is Altepa: the page's own route note for the Chamber of Oracles is the Western Altepa Desert (D-12) entrance of Quicksand Caves. That is a resolution of names the page assumed I knew, not an import of steps, and it is what gives this mission any stepping at all. Flagged ki_names_from_res so a human can overturn it in one look.

The AND-list rides the LAST group member, the Uggalepih ???, for the same reason as Windurst 8-2: the runtime's position is a high-water maximum over a linear ladder with no group support, so one verse per member would let a player who went to Uggalepih first skip the other two and land the mark on Heavens Tower. Holding all three is what moves it. None of the three is in Reward (Rank 10, 100,000 gil, the Windurstian Flag, and the right to buy the Atma of the Full Moon).

The second BCNM fight records NO mobs. The page calls them 'a Wyvern and a Manticore' -- creature types, not entity names -- and the four Cardians in the first half ARE named, so the omission is the page's, not mine. Flagged unnamed_target.
